name: Briscola Chiamata
description: Briscola Chiamata ('Called Briscola') is the sophisticated 5-player variant of Briscolaâ€”widely considered the best form of the game. After each player receives 8 cards, an auction takes place in which the highest bidder privately 'calls' (names) a specific card. The player who holds that card becomes the Caller's secret partner for the hand, without revealing themselves. The other three form the opposing team. Card ranking and trump mechanics mirror standard Briscola.

history.origins: An Italian folk development of Briscola specifically for 5 players, solving the common problem of odd player counts. The secret-partner mechanic is found in other Italian regional games (Scala Quaranta, Scopone Scientifico).
timeline: Unknown origin: Evolved from Briscola in Italian tradition.
Present: Considered by many Italian card experts to be the most skillful form of Briscola.
history.cultural: A celebrated Italian social game. Often played at family gatherings and by the Italian diaspora worldwide.
history.evolution: The secret-partner auction system distinguishes Chiamata from all simpler Briscola variants. It introduces social deduction elementsâ€”players must infer who the Caller's partner is during play.

setup.players: Exactly five players. With six present, one sits out each deal: that player deals to the other five and takes no part until the next hand. Deal and play are counter-clockwise; the player to dealer's right speaks first in bidding and leads to the first trick.
setup.deck: 40-card Italian deck (A, 3, K, Q, J, 7, 6, 5, 4, 2 in 4 suits). OR: stripped French 52-card deck.
setup.dealing: Deal 8 cards each. No trump indicatorâ€”trump is set during the auction.

rules.objective: Caller+Partner score more trick points than the 3-player team.
rules.gameplay: Standard Briscola: no follow-suit obligation. Highest trump wins; else highest of led suit. Play all 40 cards across 8 tricks.
keyRules: The partner is SECRETâ€”even the other players don't know (until it becomes obvious from play).
Caller may call a card they hold, creating a spectacular 1v4 play.
No draw phaseâ€”all 40 cards are dealt in 5-player game.

strategy.basic: Bid conservatively with 61. Name a trump card you can communicate through (Ace of trump = 11pts instantly known).
strategy.intermediate: Secret Partner Reveal: Play non-obvious defensive moves to protect the Caller without exposing yourself too early.
strategy.advanced: Calling your own card (1v4): Only justified with a powerhouse handâ€”two or more high Aces and a strong trump sequence. The social deduction aspect of inferring the partner from early plays is the game's deepest skill.
tips: If you're the Caller's partner, protect their Acesâ€”don't compete for the same tricks.
Opponents should watch for who plays defensively around the Caller.

variations.name: Briscola Bastarda
variations.description: Variant where the partner can be anyone at the table regardless of auctionâ€”a more chaotic version.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Briscola Bastarda is noted as a related Chiamata variant; detailed engine overrides for its rule tweaks are not yet modeled.

scoring.description: 120 total card points. Caller+Partner need their bid total.
scoring.winCondition: 2-player team meets or exceeds their bid.

synthesis.shortDescription: The 5-player masterpiece of Italian card gaming. The winning bidder secretly names their partner by calling a cardâ€”a brilliant social deduction layer on top of Briscola's elegant trick mechanics.
